### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`  _(via manage_platform_settings (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/automation/queues-and-assignment-rules.mdx`  _(via manage_platform_settings (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx`  _(via manage_platform_settings (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via manage_platform_settings (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`  _(via manage_platform_settings (literal, a string literal in SETUP_NAV_CONTRIBUTIONS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `17e1d7cc75c28cc41621f270c5afa3b77a76058e` — the merge of head `2a859fb0a4c5fb680932c8a16e8d7f47d3e23b07` into base `53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 17e1d7cc75c28cc41621f270c5afa3b77a76058e && git checkout 17e1d7cc75c28cc41621f270c5afa3b77a76058e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a 2a859fb0a4c5fb680932c8a16e8d7f47d3e23b07 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a && git merge --no-ff 2a859fb0a4c5fb680932c8a16e8d7f47d3e23b07

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53257a55db953086db16e756f70b649b41debd4a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8902d697eea2ccb871387f91ba48422d5735ebc5`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: yes

Face: declaration only. The PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, and no file in the list is a published schema or a governed path (`record-recognisers --paths` on the file list decides no face, so the changeset line decides it: `--face declaration`). Reviewed: the PR's own diff against merge-base `460af0e479` (42 files, +1273 −4), card #36444 with ruling 7100386248, build plan 7101465222, claim amendment 7109049897 and dev report 7109016845, and the check-runs on the head. Code outside the diff was read but not reviewed: `form-routes.ts`, `anonymous-form-intake.ts` (spec and metadata-core), `getMetaItemsPerPackage`, `runtime-metadata-persistence.ts`, `StudioCustomizeControls.tsx`, the `/meta` write, publish and delete gates, and `default-permission-sets.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

The new public surface is the Setup nav entry `nav_public_forms` (in `group_configuration`, `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`), the component ref `forms:public-forms`, the `publicFormsSetup` block in 11 console locales and the nav label in 11 platform-object locales. All of these are additive, the declaration names them, and no route, spec key, error code or stored key moves. The id string `nav_public_forms` already exists in `studio.app.ts` (Developer → Public Forms). Translations are keyed per app, so the two entries do not collide.

The ruled points:

- **Listing rule.** The page uses the spec's own `anonymousFormIntakeCandidates`, so it does not read `sharing` a second time. Listed = candidate once `enabled` is forced on; On = candidate as served. Containers are expanded by the served list, so reading `viewKind: 'form'` items misses nothing. A form switched off answers 404: its `enabled: false` with the link kept leaves the effective candidates, and it is an explicit withdrawal in the per-package layer. The PR's live run confirms this on app-crm. The other direction does not hold (M1). The routes also judge a second condition the page never reads: a withdrawal in the per-package layer (`findPublicFormView(items, [...items, ...perPackage])`). That layer always holds the base's own document under a declared override (the `getMetaItemsPerPackage` docblock). A withdrawal is a kill switch that an override cannot re-open, and `packages/rest/src/public-form-withdrawal-effective-read.test.ts:243` pins this. A strict-parsed app document that keeps its link without `enabled: true` carries the schema's default `enabled: false`, which counts as an explicit withdrawal.
- **Permission.** Nothing can be flipped without authority. The page and the entry gate on `manage_platform_settings` in the client only. The server gates every write the switch makes on `manage_metadata` / `isSystem` (`metaSaveVerdict` on save, the same verdict on publish, `manage_metadata` on the package doors). The page's capability is not the one the server enforces (N1). In the default sets, `admin_full_access` holds both capabilities and `organization_admin` holds neither, so a holder without the page capability cannot reach the switch, and a holder without `manage_metadata` is refused 403 by the server.
- **Installed-app override.** The ADR-0146 declaration is correct. `overrideDraftBody(switched, base, basedOn)` keeps an existing declaration (with its `basedOn`), otherwise it declares `{ package: base, basedOn: installed version }` and refuses with `no-version`. The app's own package is never written: `ensureDashboardSaveTarget` routes the save to `<base>.custom`. Restore-on-switch-on deletes the pair's row only when the override equals the base after removing `_` decorations and `overrides` and forcing the switch on, so an override that also carries design changes is never deleted (the "keeps design" test confirms this). Restore does not hold across an app upgrade (S1).
- **Pending drafts.** Someone else's pending draft is never published or deleted on their behalf. The restore path checks the pair's draft on the client (`isDoc(layers.draft)` → `'pending-draft'`, nothing reset). The save path is the shared `saveAndPublishRuntimeMetadata` with `ifNoneMatch: '*'`: a `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` (`isDraftVersionConflict`: status 409 and code) returns `'pending-draft'` before any publish. A refused publish discards only the draft this call wrote.
- **Concurrency.** Two admins flipping the same way: the second save meets the first's draft (409, shown as "pending draft") or finds it already published, and the result is the same. Opposite flips: last writer wins, and each page re-reads after its flip. No version is pinned, see N2.
- **Wording and leaks.** The wording is business language, and zh-CN 「对外表单」 matches the card. The page renders only the name, the object label, the address, on/off and the actions. Password, expiry and domain settings are never shown, as the ruling requires. The list read is the admin-only `GET /meta/view`. Nothing of a form's internal config is leaked. Small wording points are in N3.

Findings:

- **M1 (must-fix):** The page can show On, and toast "visitors can fill it in", for a form the anonymous routes keep at `404 FORM_NOT_FOUND`. Switching on an installed app's form that the app itself ships switched off can never work. Path: the form is listed as Off (link and `allowAnonymous` kept, `enabled` false or omitted and parse-defaulted to false). Switch on → an override with `enabled: true` in `<base>.custom` → the effective item opens it, so the row reads On after the re-read. But the base's own document stays in the per-package layer as an explicit withdrawal, and the routes never re-open it. This breaks the module's own contract ("the routes and this page must never disagree", objectui#11545) and ruling items 8–9. It fails closed: no anonymous exposure. To fix: for a customization target whose base (`layers.code`) explicitly withdraws the candidate (same slot or slug), switching on must write nothing and say in business words that the app ships this form switched off. The row's On must not be stated for such a form. Add a test with a base shipped off (explicit `enabled: false` and absent `enabled`) where the stub's pair answers `code` as the base.
- **S1 (should-fix):** Switching back on after an app upgrade pins the old version of the form for good. This contradicts ruling item 9 ("so app upgrades still flow in") and the PR's 「重新开启且没有其它改动时，自动恢复为应用原样」. Switching off copies the whole base document at version N into the override. When the app moves to N+1, `overrideHoldsOnlySwitch(override, newBase)` is false, so the override is kept with the switch on and `basedOn: N`. The environment then serves the N copy indefinitely, and this page says nothing. To fix: when the declared `basedOn` differs from the installed version and the override is not switch-only against the current base, do not report a plain "on". Either tell the admin that the form keeps the app's earlier version (and where to restore it), or restore when the override matches the base at its declared version. Add a test for an override that is switch-only at `basedOn: 2.0.0` against a changed 3.0.0 base.
- **N1 (nit):** The page asks `manage_platform_settings`, but the server authority for every write it makes is `manage_metadata`. A custom set holding only the former sees switches that always fail with a raw 403 sentence. Asking both, or naming `manage_metadata` alongside, would align the page with the server. No privilege boundary is crossed.
- **N2 (nit):** Neither the restore's `DELETE` (which accepts `If-Match`) nor the full-document save pins the version it read. A Studio publish that lands in the milliseconds between the read and the write is overwritten or reset. A concurrent admin's in-flight switch is reported with the "unpublished changes in Studio" sentence.
- **N3 (nit):** Wording. The name falls back to the internal key (`web_to_lead`) and the object column to the API name when no label is found. Refusal toasts embed the server's raw message. "Forms are designed in Studio" points to a surface the console's Studio does not have until Part 2.
- **N4 (nit):** `PublicFormsSetupPage` has no render test for the not-allowed gate, the pending-draft toast or the row update after a flip. The logic it calls is tested in `publicForms.test.ts`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/i18n` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` is correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no authorable key, value or type is added. AGENTS.md §3 says a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is declared identically in the PR body and the changeset, and it names the nav id, the component id and the locale keys, which are the full widening the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report has `open_questions: []` and `security_findings: none`. Its two out-of-scope findings (the stale body footer, which is fixed on this head, and the #34223 nav-count overlap) are answered in the PR body's Overlap paragraph. SQL push-down: there are no data queries. The listing filters the metadata list `GET /meta/view` in the client and resolves object labels from the loaded metadata. This is a metadata read, not a record join, so there is no finding. Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, no login to name.

Tests: the stubs are realistic. The served item shape carries `_packageId`. In the stub, the pair's `layered` answers the override as `effective` and the base as `code`, which matches the live run's restore. The 409 stub carries `{ status: 409, code: 'METADATA_CONFLICT' }`, which is what `isDraftVersionConflict` reads. The ablations bite:
- dropping the forced switch-on in the listing reds "keeps a switched-off form listed";
- removing the client draft check reds the pending-draft case, because `reset` would be called;
- always saving reds the restore case;
- dropping the declaration reds the `overrides` assertion;
- the CLI pin test is red at 34 without the nav entry.

There is no case for a base shipped off (M1) or an upgraded base (S1).

Check-runs on `8902d697ee`: 58 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure, none pending.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-d8t1hm`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZeHNsF3RWcWpj7rGj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `d91c73bcad5eb93ae30c7f16ebf60ec77adbd562`
Local-runs: none
Security-touching: yes

This is the round 2 delta review for round 1 (7110340811, FAIL at `8902d697ee`). I read the one commit `8902d697ee..d91c73bcad` (16 files, +486 −29) with `git show` and `git diff`. Nothing was checked out. I read the cited code outside the diff but did not review it: `form-routes.ts` `findPublicFormView`, `anonymousFormExplicitWithdrawals` / `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn` and the `getMetaItemsPerPackage` docblock.

### ① Derived judgments

Closed items:

- **M1 (must-fix): closed.**

  `switchPublicForm` now refuses a switch-on with `PublicFormSwitchRefusal('shipped-off')` when `baseShipsFormOff(layers.code, name)` is true. It does this before `ensureDashboardSaveTarget`, so the pair is not created, and before any save or reset, whether or not an override already exists. `baseShipsFormOff` treats `enabled: false` and an absent `enabled` as off, which is how the strict-parsed document the routes judge carries it. `markShippedOff` reads each installed app's form at the same address the switch uses: the pair, whose `code` is the base's own document, or the base when the pair does not hold the form. Such a row gets `on: false` and `shippedOff: true`. The page shows "Off (switched off by its app)" and disables its switch. The tests cover both spellings, the fresh case and the already-overridden case, with nothing written and the pair not ensured. Two rendered page cases cover the row. The ablation bites: without the refusal, the fresh case saves.

  The read is not the routes' per-package list. It is the base's own document, which that list always carries under an override, so the round 1 path is closed. A residual gap is S2.

- **S1 (should-fix): closed.**

  A switch-only override from an older `basedOn` is restored when the upgraded base is otherwise unchanged (`overrideHoldsOnlySwitch` against the current base, then reset).

  Otherwise the override is kept with the switch on and `basedOn` unchanged, and the switch returns `{ kind: 'earlier-version', basedOn }`. That happens only when the save published and the declared `basedOn` differs from the installed version. The toast then says the form stays on that earlier version and that Studio's restore takes the app's current form.

  This fallback is honest. It does not claim a restore that did not happen, and the module header now says why: the earlier document cannot be read. Both upgrade cases are tested. The existing "keeps design" case was moved to `basedOn: 3.0.0` so that it still tests a same-version design override.

- **N1:** closed. The page body gates the switches on `AUTHORING_CAPABILITY` (`manage_metadata`, `useCanAuthorMetadata.ts:10`). `flip` is reachable only through the `Switch`'s `onCheckedChange`, and the switch is now `disabled` when `!canSwitch`. There is no other path in the page that writes. The server gate (`metaSaveVerdict` on save and publish, `manage_metadata` on the package doors) is still the enforcement, and it did not move.
- **N3:** closed for the switch path. A 403 maps to `refusalForbidden`, and every other server refusal maps to `refusalServer`, with the raw text sent to `console.warn`. The list-load failure still shows `formatMetadataError` (see N6).
- **N4:** closed. `PublicFormsSetupPage.test.tsx` adds six rendered cases: no Setup capability, no metadata capability, shipped off ×2, the pending-draft toast, and a server refusal shown in business words.

Findings:

- **S2 (should-fix):** The shipped-off judge copies only half of the routes' withdrawal rule, so the page can still show On, and a switch-on can toast "visitors can fill it in", for a form the routes keep at 404. A route treats a body as withdrawing a form when it keeps the link with `enabled === false` **or** `allowAnonymous === false`, matched by slot **or** slug (`anonymousFormExplicitWithdrawals`). `baseShipsFormOff` returns true only when the base would open once `enabled` is forced on, so it requires `allowAnonymous: true` in the base. Path: an app ships a form with its link and `allowAnonymous: false`, and a design override made in Studio's Customize opens anonymous access with `enabled: true`. The effective item lists On, `markShippedOff` does not mark it, and a switch-on saves and reports success, while the base's own document still withdraws it at the route. This is reachable only through a customization made outside this page, and it fails closed. Fix: judge the base by the routes' own rule, either `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn([base], effective, candidate)` or a spec-side twin of `anonymousFormExplicitWithdrawals` if metadata-core is not browser-safe, so that `allowAnonymous: false` and a slug match are covered. Add a test for an app shipping `allowAnonymous: false`.
- **N5 (nit):** `markShippedOff` makes one `layered` GET per installed-app public form, all at once (`Promise.all`, no cap), on every page load and after every flip (`nonce`). The package list is read once. This is bounded by the number of public forms of installed apps, not by the number of views, so it is not a list-wide N+1. A large environment pays one request per such form per refresh. A row whose read fails is left as served, so it can show On, although its switch-on is still refused at write time.
- **N6 (nit):** For an unparsed base (`strict: false`) that omits `enabled`, the console refuses switch-on while the routes would open the form under an override. Here the console is stricter than the routes (fail-closed). Separately, the list-load failure alert still embeds the raw server message.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged: `patch` on the three packages. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` still hold. The delta adds six keys to the declared `publicFormsSetup` block in all 11 locales. It adds no route, spec key, error code or stored key, and the changeset only gains prose bullets that match the code. Nothing outside `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/**`, the console locales and the changeset moved.

### ③ Boundary flags

There are no new open questions in the delta. SQL push-down: still no record queries. The new reads are per-form metadata layer reads (N5), not a data join.

Check-runs on `d91c73bcad`: 60 success, 12 skipped, 0 failure. `Check Changeset` was in progress at first read and concluded success.

S2 is open on this head and earns a delta review of its fix. It does not block the verdict.

Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZeHNsF3RWcWpj7rGj`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2a859fb0a4c5fb680932c8a16e8d7f47d3e23b07`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts + packages/metadata-core/src/anonymous-form-intake.ts, packages/metadata-core/src/anonymous-form-intake.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json, packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/publicForms.ts
Security-touching: yes

This is round 3. Round 2 (7112039531) was PASS at `d91c73bcad` with S2 open. This head puts published spec source in the PR's file list for the first time, so the face is now the schema face: `record-recognisers --paths` on the 48 paths returns `packages/spec/src/ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts` as the one `hits` path. The record is therefore a full one, with ④.

I read the one commit `d91c73bcad..2a859fb0a4` (21 files, +260 −152) and the whole spec file at the head, with `git show` and `git diff` only. Nothing was checked out, built or run. Code outside the diff was read but not reviewed: `form-routes.ts` (`findPublicFormView`, `resolveFormBySlug`), the CLI caller in `organization-ownership-apply.ts`, the changeset config and the package manifests. An earlier draft of this round was an input. Every claim below was checked again against the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **S2 (should-fix): closed.**

  The routes and the page now call one function object.
  - `anonymousFormIntakeWithdrawnIn` is declared once, in `packages/spec/src/ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts`, and `ui/index.ts` exports the module whole.
  - `@objectstack/metadata-core` re-exports that binding in its existing `export { … } from '@objectstack/spec/ui'` block. It keeps no copy and no wrapper.
  - `form-routes.ts` is untouched and still imports the name from metadata-core. `publicForms.ts` imports it from `@objectstack/spec/ui`.
  - The identity test in metadata-core now lists the name, and asserts with `toBe` that the module's export and the package barrel's export are the spec function.

  The inputs are equivalent for the case S2 named.
  - The routes pass each served item as `view`, each of its open candidates, and a layer made of the effective list plus the per-package list, which holds the app's own document under an override.
  - The page passes the served item (the pair's `effective`, else `code`) with its switch forced on, that item's `config` candidate, and a layer of one body: the app's own document. Both bodies are renamed to the row name, which is the served item name the routes match by.

`packages/spec/src/ui/anonymous-form-intake.ts` (hits):

  - A browser bundle: the module links no schema and has no import, so the cost is about 100 lines of pure code in a module the console already loads.
